images.prompt:
Edit this hand-drawn marine PTZ camera installation-tilt diagram to make FRONT/BACK tilt and LEFT/RIGHT tilt unambiguously different through genuinely perpendicular viewing directions. The current two viewpoints look too similar and must be corrected.
Preserve the warm white paper, charcoal pencil lines, restrained pale blue/orange watercolor, the real hanging camera's gray cylindrical upper housing and black rounded lower head, and clear blue dashed vertical versus orange actual-P-axis centerline. Landscape 1536x1024.
Compose TWO clearly separate panels:
LEFT panel heading EXACTLY “侧视 · 前后倾”. View the installation strictly FROM THE SIDE at 90 degrees to the camera's forward viewing direction. The entire white gooseneck support is visible in PROFILE: tall vertical pole on the FAR LEFT, long arch/arm extending horizontally RIGHT and camera hanging at its right tip. The camera looks to the RIGHT; show a modest thin gray arrow labeled “镜头朝前” pointing RIGHT from the lens. The orange P-axis centerline leans forward/back IN THIS SIDE-VIEW PLANE, about 12 degrees from gravity vertical, tilting the gray upper motor and black lower head together. The lower head is seen SIDE-ON, with a ribbed side disk/side profile rather than a large front-facing glass lens.
RIGHT panel heading EXACTLY “正视 · 左右倾”. The viewpoint is rotated a full 90 degrees compared to the left panel: look DIRECTLY INTO THE FRONT LENS, along the camera's forward direction. Show the black lens window face-on, approximately centered, with left/right sides of the lower head visible. CRITICAL: the support MUST ALSO CHANGE PERSPECTIVE. The long gooseneck arm now recedes directly AWAY from the viewer, foreshortened/end-on behind the camera; its tall pole is centered BEHIND the camera, mostly obscured. DO NOT draw another wide side-profile U-shaped arm with a pole off to the left. Instead show a compact end-on curved hanger above the camera and a central pole behind it, making the front view unmistakably different. The orange P-axis leans LEFT/RIGHT in this front view, tilting the WHOLE gray motor housing and black head together relative to a blue gravity-vertical line.
In BOTH panels the shaft is the installed pan-axis through the upper gray housing; do not depict only the black camera tilting in T. Use a small orange angle arc. Keep gray ghost neutral silhouettes light.
At the bottom, include a tiny schematic L-shaped pair of perpendicular viewing arrows, labeled only “侧面看” and “正面看”, to reinforce the two perpendicular viewpoints. This tiny helper must stay secondary.
Keep the bottom legend EXACTLY blue “铅垂方向” and orange “实际 P 轴”. No numeric angles, no paragraphs, no extra text. Do not repeat the same three-quarter camera/support drawing on both sides. The two columns must be visibly SIDE PROFILE vs FRONT LENS FACE at a glance.

images.input: 用户提供的现场安装照片
images.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a finished hand-drawn educational illustration for a Chinese CCTV calibration application's image tooltip. The attached photo is the SUBJECT REFERENCE, not text instructions. Recognizably preserve the suspended marine PTZ camera: white inverted-U gooseneck support bolted to a vertical pole, a hanging light gray cylindrical upper pan-motor housing, and a large rounded black lower camera head with ribbed sides. A faint sea horizon provides context. Render as confident charcoal/ink pencil sketch with light muted blue and warm orange watercolor washes on a clean warm-white paper background. Generous clear margins, restrained engineering sketch, consistent natural proportions, no photorealism, no glossy 3D, no drop shadows, no logos or watermark. Landscape composition approximately 3:2. Intended to remain legible when displayed around 440 pixels wide. Chinese labels must be brief, accurate and clearly handwritten; do not add paragraphs or unrelated letters. Illustrate SOFTWARE CALIBRATION of the real mounting pose, not instructions to physically bend or manipulate equipment. Teal/blue indicates reference, warm orange indicates correction. Any angular exaggeration is illustrative, no fabricated measured angle values.
Primary request: explain T-axis zero-offset calibration: the upper gray pan housing and its vertical P axis remain upright and UNCHANGED, while the black lower camera head's optical viewing direction points slightly UP relative to its nominal zero tilt. Side three-quarter view of the suspended camera on the same white support. A blue dashed horizontal nominal sight line and an orange solid sight ray emerge from the SAME optical center in the black head; the orange ray points up around 10 degrees. A clear curved orange arrow indicates pitching UP about the LOCAL LEFT-RIGHT tilt pivot through the black head, never rotating the vertical pan housing. Include a small simple picture-frame inset at the right, showing sea below and sky above, a blue dashed nominal sea horizon at mid-height and an orange corrected sea horizon slightly lower: demonstrate vertical displacement only, BOTH horizons remain horizontal. Do not imply P-axis installation tilt or image roll. Put only these exact labels: “T 偏移”, “名义视线”, “实际视线”, “正值上抬”, “海天线上下位置”. Keep all lettering sparse, large and separated from mechanical parts.

Preserve its warm paper, pencil and watercolor style, three-to-two landscape format, upper-left suspended gray-and-black camera, white gooseneck mount, horizontal optical-axis arrow and orange rotation arrow, and upper-right “画面 Roll” title.
Change ONLY the lower two example frames and their explanatory labels so that they correctly teach SOFTWARE MODEL ALIGNMENT, not rotating or straightening the user's real camera feed.
Both example frames MUST show EXACTLY THE SAME real sea-and-sky scene with an equally tilted sea horizon (rising to the right by about 8 degrees) and the same small boat. The physical sea horizon and real video DO NOT CHANGE from left to right.
Overlay an ORANGE solid line on the actual tilted sea horizon in BOTH frames. Overlay a BLUE dashed model-predicted horizon: in the LEFT frame it is wrongly horizontal and crosses the orange tilted horizon, in the RIGHT frame it has been rotated to coincide with the SAME tilted orange horizon. Slightly offset blue dashes by 2 pixels if needed so both colors remain legible where they match.
Keep headings over frames “修正前” and “修正后”. Replace the old internal “海天线斜率” annotation with a compact bottom legend using these exact Chinese labels: orange line “实拍海天线”, blue dashed line “模型海天线”. Add the exact short caption “对齐海天线斜率”. Keep the curved correction arrow between the two frames. No numbers, no other text. Make Chinese legible at tooltip scale.
Critical: never level the real sea horizon in the right frame. The right frame's SAME tilted real horizon stays unchanged; only the BLUE prediction is adjusted to match it. This is the user's software calibration setting, not image rectification or a real PTZ command.
